patterns.usage_note: Says the quality named could come from this source and no other, and treats that as its distinction: 島ならではの食材, 老舗ならではだ. It appears as ならではの before a noun and ならではだ at the end of a clause. だけ and のみ fence off a quantity without judging it, while ならでは carries a positive or characterizing claim, which is why it fills tourism copy, menus and reviews.

examples.ruby: 生[なま]の演奏[えんそう]ならではの迫力[はくりょく]に、客席[きゃくせき]が静[しず]まり返[かえ]った。
examples.english: The hall fell silent before a force only live playing can carry.

examples.ruby: 島[しま]ならではの食材[しょくざい]を使[つか]った料理[りょうり]が並[なら]んだ。
examples.english: Out came dishes built on ingredients you can only get on the island.

examples.ruby: 隅々[すみずみ]まで行[い]き届[とど]いた気配[きくば]りは老舗[しにせ]ならではだ。
examples.english: That attention to every last detail is the mark of an old establishment.

patterns.usage_note: Limits a thing, action or state to the one named and excludes the rest: 水だけ飲む, 焼くだけだ. It attaches to nouns, plain-form verbs and adjectives, and to た. のみ makes the same restriction in written register, っきり adds a sense of meagreness to counted amounts, and ならでは praises what is exclusive rather than merely restricting. だけ also measures extent instead of restricting it (できるだけ, 好きなだけ).

examples.ruby: 今日[きょう]は水[みず]だけ飲[の]んで一日[いちにち]を過[す]ごした。
examples.english: I got through the whole day on nothing but water.

examples.ruby: あとは焼[や]くだけだから、すぐに用意[ようい]できるよ。
examples.english: All that's left is to grill it, so it'll be ready in no time.

examples.ruby: 名前[なまえ]を呼[よ]んだだけで、犬[いぬ]は尻尾[しっぽ]を振[ふ]り始[はじ]めた。
examples.english: Just saying his name set the dog's tail going.

patterns.usage_note: Restricts to the one thing named, in written and formal register: notices, contracts, academic prose, and set forms such as 〜のみならず and ただ〜のみ. It attaches to nouns and to plain-form verbs (待つのみだ). だけ carries the same restriction in speech and additionally measures extent (できるだけ), which のみ does not; in conversation のみ sounds stiff or deliberately grand.

examples.ruby: 当[とう]ホテルの駐車場[ちゅうしゃじょう]は宿泊客[しゅくはくきゃく]のみご利用[りよう]いただけます。
examples.english: The hotel car park is for the use of guests only.

examples.ruby: 準備[じゅんび]は整[ととの]ったので、あとは結果[けっか]を待[ま]つのみだ。
examples.english: Everything is in place; all that remains is to await the result.

examples.ruby: 残[のこ]された証拠[しょうこ]はこの一枚[いちまい]の写真[しゃしん]のみであった。
examples.english: The only evidence left to us was this single photograph.

glosses: and that's the last of it
patterns.usage_note: Limits an amount to the one named and colors it as meagre, final, or intimate: 一度きり, 二人っきり, これっきり. It attaches to counted amounts, small groups and これ・それ・あれ, but not to plain-form verbs (×食べるっきり), where だけ is the only option. っきり is the doubled form heard in speech and きり the plainer variant. The separate 〜たきり pattern, with a past-form verb, marks the last thing that happened before a state set in.

examples.ruby: 会[あ]ったのは一度[いちど]っきりだが、今[いま]でもよく覚[おぼ]えている。
examples.english: We met just the one time, but I remember it well even now.

examples.ruby: 二人[ふたり]っきりで話[はな]せる場所[ばしょ]を探[さが]していた。
examples.english: I was looking for somewhere the two of us could talk alone.

examples.ruby: お菓子[かし]はこれっきりだからねと母[はは]に言[い]われた。
examples.english: That's the last of the sweets, my mother told me.
